chunks: But when the truth came to them from Us, they said: 'Why is he not given the like of what was given to Moses?' Did they not disbelieve before in what was given to Moses? They said: 'Both are imposters one like the other,' and added: 'We do not believe in either.'

key_terms.تَظَاهَرَا: They supported each other / appeared mutually confirming

ai.seo_question: Why did the Israelites reject the truth when it came to them despite the miracles of Moses?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the pattern of *su' al-zann* (expecting the best for oneself while doubting the truth) where the Israelites demanded Muhammad receive the same specific miracles as Moses, despite having rejected Moses' clear proofs. Their claim that the two sets of signs were 'magic supporting each other' reflects a strategic dismissal of divine authority to preserve their own status, a theme often linked to the concept of *taqiyya* or strategic concealment in their dealings with prophets. This narrative serves as a warning against the stubbornness of those who recognize the truth but reject it due to pride or tribal loyalty.
